newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Feb 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - Feb 2.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- PRU AND FORTIS WOOING SCOT AM

The Prudential and Fortis, the Belgian/Dutch insurance group, are poised to make rival bids for mutual life insurer Scottish Amicable. Fortis is expanding aggressively by making takeovers in the banking sector and acquired merchant bank Mees Pierson from ABN Amro. Tthe National Westminster Bank and Halifax Building Society may also be interested in Scot Am.
-- LONDON TARGET FOR 25 BILLION STG OLD MUTUAL EXPANSION

South Africa's biggest insurer, Old Mutual, is preparing a hit list of fund management companies as part of an expansion programme to make London the centre of a new 25 billion stg asset management operation. The company plans to buy UK-based fund management firms ahead of the dismantling of South Africa's exchange controls.
-- TRIPLEX DEMANDS DTI PROBE

Bob Mitchell, finance director at Triplex Lloyd, has confirmed that the group has approached the DTI with a request for an insider dealing investigation into steel castings group William Cook. The inquiry centres on a share buy back involving 5.5 per cent of Cook shares three days after the group issued a profits warning.
-- EXCHANGE VETS HOGG DEALING

The Stock Exchange is investigating share dealings by Clive Holmes, a director of travel group Hogg Robinson. A profit warning last Tuesday meant that 25 per cent was wiped off the group's share price.
-- ASPINALL BRINGS CASH SHELL TO AIM

Damian Aspinall is set to test the Alternative Investment Market with its first pure cash shell. Dealings are set to begin in Calidore Group, a company he set up to back his deal-making hunches and those of Anton Bilton. Fiske & Co, stockbroker, has placed shares and warrants at 2.5 pence in Calidore to raise an initial fund of two million stg. The aim is to invest cash in smaller companies with opportunities to float in the medium term and use shares to go into larger companies.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- VICKERS GUNS FOR THREE BILLION STG TANK ORDER IN TURKEY

Vickers is set to launch a campaign to win Britain's biggest-ever overseas order for armoured ground vehicles. The company aims to defeat international rivals for a three billion stg order from Turkey for 800 battle tanks. Vickers faces a harder struggle to win a 750 million stg order for 200 tanks from Saudi Arabia.
-- SAINSBURY CHAIRMAN: 'I'M IN THE FIRING LINE'

Chairman of supermarket group Sainsbury, David Sainsbury, has acknowledged the pressure he is facing from shareholders, including members of his own family. In his first interview since the grocer's profit warning nine days ago he said, "I am in the firing line". Analysts in the City have been speculating that he may choose to relinquish executive duties or leave altogether.
-- FEARS GROW OF COLLAPSE IN JAPAN

Business leaders have been meeting in Switzerland for the annual World Economic Forum. They were warned this weekend that financial turbulence could upset the benign outlook for the world economy. Experts claim that turbulence was most likely to come in Europe where any disappointment over progress towards monetary union would hit bond markets hard, and in Japan, where the financial system is so fragile it may be in danger of collapsing.
-- LONDON CLUBS ROLLS THE DICE FOR CROCKFORDS

Casino group London Clubs International has put in a 175 million stg bid for rival Capital Corporation, which owns two of London's top clubs, Crockfords and the Colony. Chief executive of London Clubs, Alan Goodenough, is believed to have made the approach as a spoiling tactic. London Clubs is also under threat of a takeover approach, possibly from Ladbroke.
-- FIRST DIRECT DIALS UP SCOTS JOBS

Midland Bank's telephone-banking division, First Direct, is close to finalising a deal to build a huge call centre in Scotland. The multi-million-pound investment is expected to create more than 2,000 jobs in the region. The region was chosen because research has shown that the Scottish accent is trustworthy and friendly, which is well-suited to telephone- banking transactions.
THE OBSERVER
-- 2,000 MORE FORD JOBS FACE THE CHOP

Ford's transit van factory in Southampton could face closure. Production of a new Transit Van could be moved to Belgium to stem financial losses. The threat comes after the announcement Ford would not build the new Escort at Halewood and 1,300 workers would lose their jobs.
-- BRITISH BUSINESSES BACK TOYOTA BOSS'S INVESTMENT WARNING

Toyota Motor president Hiroshi Okunda's warning that jobs and future investment will drain from the UK if it stays outside a single European currency has been supported by leading British businessmen, including Unilever, British Aerospace and Unigate. Some of them also expressed worries about the costs of currency fluctuations between the countries that joined and those staying out.
-- CELTIC PLAYING AT ANFIELD? IT COULD HAPPEN

Football sponsor Coca-Cola is attempting to persuade the Football League to allow Scottish and English clubs to compete in the same domestic competition, called the 'British League Cup'. The news will fuel the share frenzy surrounding English and Scottish football stocks as clubs flock to the City.
-- DIGITAL TV DEAL BRINGS 400 MILLION STG DOWN TO EARTH

The consortium known as British Digital Broadcasting, the new digital terrestrial television services planned by BSkyB, Granada, Carlton and the BBC, is set to generate 400 million stg a year in subscription revenues, with BDB planning to charge five pounds per month per subscriber for its 12 basic channels.
-- REGULATOR SLAMS RAIL UNDERSPEND

John Swift, rail regulator, has admitted that he has no power to force Railtrack to invest more in the nations network. He said that it was unacceptable for the privatised track, signalling and stations owner to have underspent its 3.5 billion stg maintenance budget by 700 million stg. If he wants to punish the company he must wait four years for the first pricing review after privatisation.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- BIG ITALIAN MATCH IS OFF

Bankers and investors believe that the prospects of all but a minority of Italian football clubs listing their shares on the London Stock Exchange are very remote. Commercial and legal obstacles may stop moves by some top British clubs if they want to create ties with the continental elite by taking cross- shareholdings in each other.
-- MMC IN FIRING LINE OVER BASS PROBE

The Monopolies and Mergers Commission is involved in a row over Sir Archibald Foster, a senior member of its team investigating Bass's 200 million stg takeover of rival Carlsberg- Tetley. He is a non-executive of director of Midland Bank, as is Tony Hales, chief executive of Allied Domecq, which sold one half of Carlsberg-Tetley. Some industry figures believe this working relationship should mean that Sir Foster should stand down from the investigation.
-- ITT RECONSIDERS LADBROKE BID

Sheraton hotels and Caesar's World casinos group, ITT, is considering a bid for Ladbroke in an effort to ward off a hostile bid from Hilton Hotels. Aborted talks last February could pave the way for ITT to launch a poison-pill bid for Ladbroke without incurring the wrath of shareholders in the US courts.
-- DTI TO TARGET PYRAMID CROOKS

New regulations are being put into place to outlaw crooked pyramid selling scams operating from overseas, as well as the UK. The new penalty, of up to two years in jail, will now apply to more than just the promoters. Everyone who joins and attempts to recruit others will be committing a criminal offence. The DTI are currently concerned that directors of the banned Alchemy UK scheme are operating a new scam from a base in Amsterdam.
-- EU TO ACT ON BSKYB SPORT

European Commission is set to curb the growing power of cable and satellite TV firms, such as BSkyB, from snapping up important live sports events. The proposals will ensure that viewers across Europe will not be charged to view prestige national sporting events.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- NASDAQ LAUNCHES TV ADS BLITZ IN BRITAIN

New York's Nasdaq exchange is set to spend 6.5 million stg advertising on British television to lure UK investors and companies to its stock market, which is America's second largest. Nasdaq is spending on the same scale as car companies when a new model is launched. Bill Gates of Microsoft and Andy Grove of Intel are being used to promote Nasdaq's World Wide Web site on the Internet.
-- OFSKY THREAT FOR MURDOCH

Labour politicians have been warned that Rupert Murdoch could be poised to control digital television on both satellite and terrestrial networks and that it could be necessary to curb his power by appointing a regulator, called OfSky. OfSky would control the price other broadcasters would have to pay for access to digital technology owned by Murdoch. Its remit would be to ensure that the BBC and ITV were left with enough cash to maintain the quality of their programmes.
-- BSKYB LET OFF THE 100 MILLION STG TAX HOOK

The Labour Party have said that BSkyB will not have to pay a 100 million stg levy if Labour wins power. The party has ruled out a tax on profits over and above its normal corporate liability. The City had assumed that a Blair-led government would be hostile to BSkyB because of Labour's alleged dislike of Rubert Murdoch.
-- BILL FOR EURO TO BE 'LESS THAN EXPECTED'

A survey for the International Securities and Markets Association reveals that the cost to the financial sector of conversion to a single European currency will be lower than expected. Banks, securities houses and other financial institutions across Europe will face an average bill of only about 137,000 stg to convert their systems to the Euro.
-- ORDERS RISING FOR SMALL FIRMS

A report by the CBI suggests that small and medium manufacturing firms are winning more orders and creating more jobs than their larger rivals. It will show that while big manufacturing companies are cutting their workforces, smaller firms are taking on new staff. Companies shedding staff outnumbered those recruiting by 11 points in the manufacturing sector as a whole. BMC +44-171-377-1742
